title: Radio operating controls
blurb: Set squelch, filters, RIT, mic gain and digital-radio settings so you can hear and be heard clearly.

T4B01.why: Past the transmitter's limit the audio peaks are flattened, giving **distorted transmitted audio**.
T4B01.trap: Gain affects audio quality, not frequency stability or SWR.

T4B02.why: You enter a frequency with the **keypad or the VFO knob**.
T4B02.trap: CTCSS and DTMF are tones, not frequency entry.

T4B03.why: Squelch mutes signals below its threshold. For weak signals, lower it so **audio is on all the time**.
T4B03.trap: Turning up audio volume does not beat the squelch gate.

T4B04.why: FM demodulation expects a centered signal. Off frequency, the audio comes out **distorted**.
T4B04.trap: Pitch shifting is an SSB effect, not FM.

T4B05.why: Scanning **tunes through a range of frequencies to check for activity**.

T4B06.why: On SSB, being off frequency shifts the voice pitch. **RIT or the Clarifier** moves receive tuning to fix it.
T4B06.trap: AGC, bandwidth and tone squelch do not change pitch.

T4B07.why: A code plug is **configuration data** loaded into your radio to reach repeaters and talkgroups.
T4B07.trap: It's data, not a cable, an upgrade or a CODEC.

T4B08.why: Choose a bandwidth that **matches the mode** to reduce noise and interference.

T4B09.why: On DMR you select a group by entering its **ID code**.
T4B09.trap: CTCSS tones are analog FM, not DMR.

T4B10.why: An SSB voice signal is about 2.4 kHz wide, so **2400 Hz** passes it all with the least extra noise.
T4B10.trap: 500 Hz cuts the voice; 5000 Hz admits extra noise.

T4B11.why: A D-STAR radio must be programmed with **your call sign** before it transmits.
